correctness.rationale: The exact affine chord formula is obtained by pulling a support line back to the unit disk and multiplying the disk half-chord by the two-dimensional affine stretch factor. Antipodal subtraction isolates a linear center form over the square of the shape quadratic. For nonzero centers, equality gives a homogeneous polynomial identity; irreducibility of positive-definite binary quadratics and unique factorization force proportional shape forms, determinant scaling then forces equal centers, and the full data remove the scalar. A zero center forces the other center to vanish. The centered branch is exhausted by the same factor argument plus a separate scalar-circle case. The packaged checker independently verifies the formula and odd identity on deterministic examples.

value.rationale: The unrestricted planar one-disk problem is a longstanding geometric-tomography question, and arbitrary ellipses are the canonical full smooth quadratic subclass with free translation and anisotropy. The theorem gives a global, nonperturbative answer on this natural five-parameter class. Its key mechanism is structural--antipodal data split translation from an irreducible quadratic shape factor--rather than a routine numerical or coordinate-table computation.
